course_name_original: Teoría de estructuras y construcciones industriales
course_name_en: Theory of Structures and Industrial Constructions

learning_outcomes.text: To have systematic knowledge and understanding of the key concepts and aspects for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
To be able to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve problems in the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions using established methods.
To be able to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods in the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
To have an understanding of the different methods for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions and the ability to use them.
To be able to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other sources of information.
To be able to combine theory and practice to solve problems in the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.
To have an understanding of applicable methods and techniques in the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions and their limitations.
To be aware of all the implications of engineering practice.

To demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.
A systematic understanding of the key concepts and aspects of their engineering branch.
The ability to apply their knowledge and understanding to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems using established methods.
The ability to choose and apply relevant analytical and modeling methods.
Understanding of different methods and the ability to use them.
The ability to perform bibliographic searches, use databases and other sources of information.
The ability to combine theory and practice to solve engineering problems.
Understanding of applicable methods and techniques and their limitations.
Awareness of all the implications of engineering practice.
Demonstrate awareness of the responsibility of engineering practice, its social and environmental impact, and commitment to professional ethics, responsibility and standards of engineering practice.

Students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually found at a level that, while supported by advanced textbooks, also includes aspects involving knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

Students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competences that are usually demonstrated by means of the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their field of study.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Ability to design a system, component or process in the field of mechanical engineering to meet the required specifications.
Knowledge and ability to apply current legislation as well as mandatory specifications, regulations and standards in the field of mechanical engineering.
Knowledge and ability to apply computational and experimental tools for the analysis and quantification of mechanical engineering problems.
Knowledge and ability for the calculation and design of structures and industrial constructions.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the calculation of metallic structures
teaching_methods: Laboratory practices in specific hours in small groups
Online SPOC course (with videos and exercises)
assessment_rules: For continuous assessment to be taken into account, a score of 4.5 or higher must be obtained in the final exam, both in the ordinary and extraordinary calls. To pass the course, attendance and completion of the laboratory practices planned in the weekly schedule are mandatory. The weighting of the practical grade in the continuous assessment corresponds to what is established in the course, in accordance with the university's regulations. In this course, the weighting of laboratory practices is 10% of the continuous assessment grade.
